current.summary: Architecture-first session, at the user’s direction. The three entry-flow bugs the handset found were not three bugs but one absence: the flow had never been specified as a process, and all three failures were at the joins between screens that each had passing tests. Wrote docs/entry-flow.md as the normative spec — use cases, DFD level 2, state machine, launch decision, an exhaustive OTP callback contract, and 13 invariants each naming its test — then fixed the code against it. Writing the spec surfaced three further defects nobody had reported. 307 tests to 339, analyze clean. Nothing has been on the handset yet.
current.state: Entry flow specified and fixed in code, pinned by 32 new tests; not yet verified on the Galaxy S24 — that is next session’s first job. Phases 0-3.5 complete on real hardware; real SMS works; VPS is a Spot VM Azure keeps deallocating; no backend yet
decisions: Architecture before code, at the user’s explicit instruction. Writing the spec first is what surfaced the three additional defects — none was on the bug list

Instant verification is accepted and skips the code screen. "Every fresh login goes through OTP" means there is no password, not that a message must be billed on every entry — the platform performs the same possession check against the same SIM. It still cannot skip consent

Cold start only for locking. A warm resume does not lock: a fingerprint prompt every time someone checks a notification is the most common reason people switch biometrics off, and a backgrounded app is already behind the OS lock screen
A returning member never sees /welcome. It is a marketing screen, and the Android system splash already covers the moment before the first frame
No consent card on a returning sign-in — an unticked optional box on a screen the member did not open to change anything is a withdrawal they never made

The launch decision lives in the router, not in SplashScreen.initState: a screen that decides where to go is only consulted when that screen is built, and that is precisely the screen a member must not be shown
locationAsked mirrors biometricOffered — false and never-asked are different states and only one should produce a screen
Every invariant names its test. A rule with nothing in the right-hand column is a comment, not a standard
working: Cannot sign in a second time: verificationCompleted resolved nothing, so on a repeat sign-in Firebase instant-verified the SIM and send() never returned. Fixed and pinned, with a 60s backstop against any future unhandled callback
Biometric unlock never engages: nothing in lib/ navigated to Routes.unlock. Fixed by the launch decision in the router
Reopen falling back to SMS then too-many-requests: same root cause — the welcome screen made no launch decision
Three further defects found while specifying and fixed: resend did not resend; signing in overwrote consent; a refused location was re-asked on every entry
The code-discovery skill is committed and pushed here (d783e12); the running copy at ~/.claude/skills is identical bar the five-line canonical-source banner
notWorking: NONE OF IT HAS BEEN ON THE HANDSET. This matters more than usual here: the whole argument of entry-flow.md §8.2 is that a green suite proves nothing about reachability. Next session’s first job
The 60s no-hang backstop has no test — it needs fake_async or an injectable duration. Every other row of the callback table is covered
The typed-code confirm half has still never been seen succeeding in a real log
No backend: a sent request never becomes a booking, a review is dropped
The VPS is a Spot VM so Azure will keep stopping it
Three brand cuts and one logo still exceed the 256 KiB fetch cap
doNotRepeat: A quoted bash heredoc fails in this environment on content containing apostrophes — twice, with "unexpected EOF while looking for matching ’". Use the Write tool, or a Python script in the scratchpad. Do not keep retrying
grep "\.lock()" inside double quotes silently matched nothing and I briefly said lock() had zero callers. It has four, all in tests. Escaping inside double quotes is not escaping inside single quotes
dart format lib test reformatted six files the session never touched. The repo is not fully formatted, so a blanket format inflates the diff with unrelated churn
ref.read(provider.notifier).state is not how to read back a mutation — use ref.read(provider) after the call

Carried: a seam that discards the cause is not observable; a test that constructs the state it tests cannot prove the state is reachable; do not conclude from a search; local_auth 3.x is not 2.x; never transcribe a binary
nextSteps: Run the whole entry flow on the Galaxy S24, debug build: register, kill and reopen (must land on /unlock, never /welcome), unlock by fingerprint, sign out, sign in again — that last one is the instant-verification path
Watch for "otp: confirm accepted" — the typed-code confirm half has never been seen succeeding in a real log
Decide whether the 60s backstop earns a test; fake_async in dev_dependencies is the smaller change
Deal with the VPS deallocation before Phase 4 puts a ledger on it
Phase 4: becoming a provider, paired with the admin queue
Tick the remaining 27 screens element by element
Send design/CORRECTIONS.md to the design side — nine entries now, two new
blockers: From entry-flow.md §10, all genuinely undecided: account recovery when the number is gone; whether a second handset should end the first session; what rate limit is ours once an aggregator replaces Firebase’s unpublished throttle; whether /unlock should add a lockout on top of the OS’s
BLOCKED, user-only: four brand files exceed the 256 KiB get_file cap
Undesigned: the dispute FLOW, messaging, the calling screens, empty and offline states, profile photos

Five rounds of user pushback, each correct: the design project was reachable all along; only one canvas of five had been read; docs must precede Dart; wrong documentation is an emergency because everything downstream inherits it; and the flattener was stripping <script>, which is where the design keeps PAL, CATS, REQUIREMENTS and all eleven BSTATES. Brand imported and shipped - launcher, adaptive, splash and notification icons all real and verified on device. Colour and type verified against the canvas rather than assumed. Booking status built with all eleven states.

Followed docs/build-order.md rather than re-deriving it. Closed Phase 0 by running all five built screens on a Pixel 9a in both modes - the first time this app has been seen rendered. The palette came back exact; the supply count was ellipsised and is fixed. The run exposed that the app has no identity at all, raised by the user mid-session: stock Flutter icon, white cold-start flash, no mark. Fixed what needed no artwork, made the rest an enforced artifact. Then built Phase 1 in full: seven entry routes plus the auth gate, with the entry rules held as states in core/session.dart. 147 tests.
